Reasoning: Since the upper output terminal is positive relative to the lower terminal, conventional current flows from the positive terminal of the 18 V power supply through R to the upper node on the right side, and then enters the series branch of the two Zener diodes. According to the relative directions of the two Zener diodes in the figure, one Zener diode is in the reverse breakdown voltage-stabilizing state, with a voltage drop of UZ=5.3 V; the other is in the forward conduction state, with a forward voltage drop of 0.7 V. The voltage across the two ends of the series branch is the output voltage U0, therefore U0=5.3 V+0.7 V=6.0 V.

With the top output node positive relative to the bottom node, trace conventional current from the 18 V source through R into the diode string. From the diode symbols, identify that one Zener is driven into reverse breakdown while the other is forward biased. Replace the reverse-biased Zener by a 5.3 V drop and the forward-biased diode by a 0.7 V drop. Add the two series drops across the output branch: U0 = 5.3 V + 0.7 V = 6.0 V.
